The '''2021–22 Ohio University Bobcats men's basketball team''' represented [[Ohio University]] for the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Bobcats were led by third-year head coach [[Jeff Boals]], who was a 1995 graduate of Ohio University.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/coaches/index|title=Men's Basketball|website=Ohio University|language=en|access-date=2019-10-16|archive-date=2019-10-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191016173856/https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/coaches/index|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/coaches/jeff-boals-1.html|title=Jeff Boals|website=Sports Reference|language=en|access-date=2022-09-29}}</ref> The team played their home games at the [[Convocation Center (Ohio University)|Convocation Center]] in [[Athens, Ohio]] as a member of the [[Mid-American Conference]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ohio.edu/building-directory/convocation-center|title=Convocation Center|website=Ohio University|language=en|access-date=2022-09-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://getsomemaction.com/standings.aspx?standings=153|title=2021-22 Men's Basketball Standings|website=Mid-American Conference|language=en|access-date=2022-11-11}}</ref>

Ohio completed non-conference play with a record of 9–2 with wins over [[Ohio Valley Conference|OVC]] favorite<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.belmontbruins.com/sports/m-baskbl/2021-22/releases/20211016phb8xc|title=OVC Preseason Poll|website=Belmont University|language=en|access-date=2022-01-11}}</ref> [[Belmont Bruins men's to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401365016|title=No. 13 Kentucky shakes off early rust to beat Ohio 77-59|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-11-13}}</ref> and [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401365044|title=Eason, Days lead LSU to 66-51 victory over Ohio|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-11-13}}</ref> Ohio opened conference play 5–0 to extend their winning streak to nine games.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401365115|title=Vander Plas scores 23 to lift Ohio over Miami (Ohio) 86-63|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-02-05}}</ref> Ohio lost to [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]] in the next game and fell into second place in the MAC standings.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401365125|title=Rollins scores 25 to lift Toledo past Ohio 87-69|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-02-05}}</ref> After a win against [[Western Michigan Broncos men's basketball|Western Michigan]], Ohio regained first place with a conference record of 10–1. With an overall record of 19–3, they stood alone in [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball|Ohio basketball]] history for the best record after 22 games.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://suacbobcats.com/2022/02/05/bobcats-make-history-behind-carter-beat-wmu-77-64/|title=Bobcats Make History Behind Carter, Beat WMU 77-64|website=SUACBobcats|language=en|access-date=2022-02-05|first=Jason|last=Arkley}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401365149|title=Carter's double-double leads Ohio over W. Michigan 77-64|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-02-05}}</ref> Their five-game winning streak was snapped in the following game with a second loss to Toledo which left both teams with two losses in MAC conference play.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401365154|title=Millner Jr., Shumate lift Toledo over Ohio 77-62|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-02-13}}</ref> After three consecutive wins following the Toledo loss, the Bobcats then lost 4 out of their last 5 conference games and finished the regular season 23–8 and 14–6 in conference play which was tied for third place in the MAC. During the lone win with that five game stretch, starting [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] [[Ben Vander Plas]] scored the fourth triple double in program history in a win against [[2021–22 Central Michigan Chippewas men's basketball team|Central Michigan]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=VANDER PLAS LIFTS OHIO OVER CENTRAL MICHIGAN 76-50|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/vander-plas-lifts-ohio-over-central-michigan-76-50/|access-date=May 14, 2022|website=CBS Sports|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Vander Plas lifts Ohio over Central Michigan 76-50|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/vander-plas-lifts-ohio-central-michigan-76-50-83053137|access-date=September 6, 2022|website=ABC|language=en}}</ref> After the regular season Vander Plas was named the [[List of Men's Basketball Academic All-America Team Members of the Year|Division I Academic All-American of the Year]]<ref name = "RealGM">{{cite web |title=NCAA Division I Basketball Awards|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/awards/109/Academic-All-American-Team-Member-of-the-Year|website=RealGM|access-date=September 12, 2022}}</ref>

After defeating [[Ball State Cardinals men's basketball|Ball State]] in the quarterfinals, the Bobcats lost to [[Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball|Kent State]] in the semi-finals of the [[2022 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401405869|title=Sears leads Ohio over Ball State 77-67 in MAC tourney|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-09-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://ohiobobcats.com/news/2022/3/11/mens-basketball-ohio-drops-semifinal-contest-against-kent-state.aspx|title=Ohio Drops Semifinal Contest Against Kent State|website=Ohio University Athletics|language=en|access-date=2022-03-12}}</ref> Ohio was the #3 seed in the [[2022 College Basketball Invitational|CBI]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2954363-cbi-2022-tournament-bracket-schedule-format-and-teams-to-watch|title=CBI 2022: Tournament Bracket, Schedule, Format and Teams to Watch|website=Bleacher Report|language=en|access-date=2022-09-30}}</ref> They defeated [[2021–22 Rice Owls men's basketball team|Rice]] in the first round before losing to [[2021–22 Abilene Christian Wildcats men's basketball team|Abilene Christian]] in the second round.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401411723|title=Sears lifts Ohio past Rice on late shot|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-09-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401411731|title=Ohio 86, Abilene Christian 91|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-09-30}}</ref>

==Previous season==

{{main|2020–21 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team}}

In a season limited due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], the [[2020–21 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|Bobcats]] finished the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]] 17–8, 9–5 in [[2020–21 Mid-American Conference men's basketball season|MAC play]] to finish in fourth place. As the No. 5 seed in the [[2021 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]], they defeated [[2020–21 Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball team|Kent State]], [[2020–21 Toledo Rockets men's basketball team|Toledo]], and [[2020–21 Buffalo Bulls men's basketball team|Buffalo]] to win the tournament championship. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 13 seed in the West region.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2020-21/schedule|title=2020–21 Ohio Men's Basketball Schedule|website=Ohio University|language=en|access-date=2021-09-03}}</ref> There they upset No. 4-seeded [[2020–21 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC champion]] [[2020–21 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the first round<ref>{{cite web |title=Ohio vs. Virginia – Game Recap – March 20, 2021 – ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401310926|access-date=2021-10-25|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> before losing to No. 5-seeded [[2020–21 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] in the second round.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ohio vs. Creighton – Game Recap – March 22, 2021 – ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401310890|access-date=2021-10-25|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/news/2021/03/22/ohio-university-athens-court-street-march-madness-creighton-game/4797106001/|first=Megan|last=Henry|title=Athens celebrated March Madness game — despite outcome|website=The Columbus Dispatch|language=en|access-date=2021-09-03}}</ref>
